case_notes:
# Case 6

Provisional diagnosis: myeloid neoplasm, unspecified.

72F with persistent macrocytic anaemia. Bone marrow is reported as showing
insufficient dysplastic change for a diagnosis of MDS. Blasts are not increased.
Iron stain shows 7% ring sideroblasts.

NGS (myeloid panel):
- SF3B1 pathogenic variant, VAF 30%

structured_case.detected_variants_summary: NGS detected an SF3B1 pathogenic variant (VAF 30%).

case_facts.value: Bone marrow has insufficient dysplastic change for a diagnosis of MDS; blasts are not increased.

It intentionally does not encode transcript, exon, or amplicon numbers.

## Negative-result semantics

When the patient NGS result is explicitly complete, a listed panel gene that is absent from the detected-variant list is interpreted as **no SNV, short insertion/deletion, or short-range complex variant detected in that gene within the validated assay scope**.

Use this negative result when applying diagnostic, prognostic, biomarker, treatment, germline, and other reporting rules. Do not treat the gene as unresolved merely because it is not individually listed in the patient result.

This inference is limited to the assay scope. It does not establish whole-gene biological wild type and does not exclude copy-number changes, rearrangements, structural variants, or other variant classes unless the patient result or another supplied test explicitly assesses them.

If the patient NGS result is described as partial, selected, limited, abbreviated, pending, or otherwise incomplete, do not infer a negative result for an unlisted panel gene.

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML with an in-frame bZIP CEBPA mutation can be diagnosed with at least 10% blood or marrow blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML with BCR::ABL1 retains a blast requirement of at least 20%.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: The MDS/AML category is not used for BCR::ABL1-positive AML because of overlap with progression of BCR::ABL1-positive CML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: ASXL1 mutation qualifies for MDS/AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at 10%-19% blasts or AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: BCOR mutation qualifies for MDS/AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at 10%-19% blasts or AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: EZH2 mutation qualifies for MDS/AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at 10%-19% blasts or AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: RUNX1 mutation qualifies for MDS/AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at 10%-19% blasts or AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: SF3B1 mutation qualifies for MDS/AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at 10%-19% blasts or AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: SRSF2 mutation qualifies for MDS/AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at 10%-19% blasts or AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: STAG2 mutation qualifies for MDS/AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at 10%-19% blasts or AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: U2AF1 mutation qualifies for MDS/AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at 10%-19% blasts or AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: ZRSR2 mutation qualifies for MDS/AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at 10%-19% blasts or AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutation at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In AML classification, single-gene mutation or gene-fusion categories take precedence over myelodysplasia-related gene-mutation and myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic categories.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Pure erythroid leukemia is typically TP53-mutated and is classified within AML with TP53 mutation in the ICC.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: The remaining AML categories retain a blast requirement of at least 20%.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS cases with 10%-19% blasts are classified as MDS/AML after higher-priority AML-defining genetic categories are considered.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ICC Classification of Myeloid Neoplasms and Acute Leukemias

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In MDS, TP53 multihit status is defined by multiple TP53 mutations or by a TP53 mutation with loss of heterozygosity, including chromosomal deletion or copy-neutral LOH.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: IPSS-M Prognostic score for MDS

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML classification is hierarchical: AML with a recurrent genetic abnormality takes precedence; among remaining categories, TP53-mutated disease supersedes myelodysplasia-related gene-mutated disease, which supersedes myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic disease.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For categories other than AML-defining recurrent genetic abnormalities, 10%-19% marrow or blood blasts are designated MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts are designated AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Cases with a prior MPN are excluded from AML classification at 10%-19% blasts and are classified as accelerated-phase MPN; at at least 20% blasts they are classified as blast-phase MPN.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For patients with an established MDS/MPN, the MDS/MPN diagnosis is retained until there are at least 20% blasts/blast equivalents; detection of an AML-defining recurrent genetic abnormality at 10%-19% blasts does not itself change that diagnostic label.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: t(15;17)(q24.1;q21.2)/PML::RARA defines APL/AML with at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: t(8;21)(q22;q22.1)/RUNX1::RUNX1T1 defines AML with at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: inv(16)(p13.1q22) or t(16;16)(p13.1;q22)/CBFB::MYH11 defines AML with at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: t(9;11)(p21.3;q23.3)/MLLT3::KMT2A defines AML with at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: t(6;9)(p22.3;q34.1)/DEK::NUP214 defines AML with at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: inv(3)(q21.3q26.2) or t(3;3)(q21.3;q26.2)/GATA2,MECOM(EVI1) defines AML with at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Mutated NPM1 is an AML-defining recurrent genetic abnormality when marrow or blood blasts are at least 10%.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: An in-frame mutation in the CEBPA bZIP domain, monoallelic or biallelic, defines the CEBPA-mutated AML subtype when marrow or blood blasts are at least 10%.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML with t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2)/BCR::ABL1 requires at least 20% marrow or blood blasts; cases with BCR::ABL1 rearrangement and 10%-19% blasts are classified as CML in accelerated phase.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), recurrent RARA rearrangements involving IRF2BP2, NPM1, ZBTB16, STAT5B, STAT3, TBL1XR1, FIP1L1, or BCOR should be reported as the specific RARA-rearranged entity; as AML-defining recurrent abnormalities, they apply at at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute myeloid leukemia (AML), recurrent KMT2A rearrangements with AFF1, AFDN, MLLT10, TET1, ELL, or MLLT1 should be reported as the specific KMT2A-rearranged entity; as AML-defining recurrent abnormalities, they apply at at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute myeloid leukemia (AML), recurrent MECOM rearrangements involving MYC, ETV6, RUNX1, or the listed t(2;3) MECOM rearrangement should be reported as the specific MECOM-rearranged entity; as AML-defining recurrent abnormalities, they apply at at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute myeloid leukemia (AML), the rare recurring rearrangements involving PRDM16::RPN1, RBM15::MRTFA, NPM1::MLF1, NUP98::NSD1, ETV6::MNX1, KAT6A::CREBBP, PICALM::MLLT10, NUP98::KMD5A or other NUP98 partners, FUS::ERG, RUNX1::CBFA2T3, and CBFA2T3::GLIS2 are AML-defining recurrent genetic abnormalities and apply at at least 10% marrow or blood blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In the absence of an overriding AML-defining recurrent genetic abnormality, a pathogenic somatic TP53 mutation with VAF at least 10%, with or without loss of the wild-type TP53 allele, defines the TP53-mutated category; cases are MDS/AML at 10%-19% blasts and AML at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute myeloid leukemia (AML) lacking an overriding recurrent AML abnormality and TP53 mutation, mutations in ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, RUNX1, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1, or ZRSR2 define the myelodysplasia-related gene-mutated category irrespective of prior MDS; these cases are designated MDS/AML at 10%-19% blasts and AML at at least 20% blasts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: At least three unrelated chromosome abnormalities, excluding class-defining recurring abnormalities and hyperdiploid karyotypes with three or more trisomies/polysomies without structural abnormalities, is a complex karyotype sufficient for the myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic AML category when higher-priority categories are absent. In this branch, 10%-19% blasts is MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts is AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: del(5q), t(5q), or add(5q) is sufficient for the myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic AML category when higher-priority categories are absent. In this branch, 10%-19% blasts is MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts is AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Monosomy 7 or del(7q) is sufficient for the myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic AML category when higher-priority categories are absent. In this branch, 10%-19% blasts is MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts is AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Trisomy 8 is sufficient for the myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic AML category when higher-priority categories are absent. In this branch, 10%-19% blasts is MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts is AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: del(12p), t(12p), or add(12p) is sufficient for the myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic AML category when higher-priority categories are absent. In this branch, 10%-19% blasts is MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts is AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: i(17q) is sufficient for the myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic AML category when higher-priority categories are absent. In this branch, 10%-19% blasts is MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts is AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Monosomy 17, add(17p), or del(17p) is sufficient for the myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic AML category when higher-priority categories are absent. In this branch, 10%-19% blasts is MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts is AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: del(20q) is sufficient for the myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic AML category when higher-priority categories are absent. In this branch, 10%-19% blasts is MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts is AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: idic(X)(q13) is sufficient for the myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic AML category when higher-priority categories are absent. In this branch, 10%-19% blasts is MDS/AML and at least 20% blasts is AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Remaining cases without a higher-priority AML-defining category are classified as AML, not otherwise specified, when blasts are at least 20%, irrespective of the presence or absence of multilineage dysplasia.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: When a germline predisposing disorder is identified, it is appended as a diagnostic qualifier to the specific genetically defined AML disease category rather than replacing that primary category.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In germline CEBPA-mutation carriers, distinct acquired CEBPA mutations can re-emerge as independent primary AMLs rather than representing relapse, so recurrence may require distinction between a new primary AML and relapse.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Prior cytotoxic chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immune intervention for a nonmyeloid neoplasm is recorded as a therapy-related diagnostic qualifier rather than defining a separate AML disease entity.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Progression from MDS is appended as a diagnostic qualifier when the antecedent MDS was confirmed by standard diagnostics more than 3 months before AML diagnosis.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Progression from MDS/MPN is appended as a diagnostic qualifier, with the MDS/MPN type specified, when the antecedent MDS/MPN was confirmed by standard diagnostics more than 3 months before AML diagnosis.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Multiparameter flow-cytometric immunophenotyping is required to diagnose AML accurately by identifying cell-surface and intracellular markers.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute myeloid leukemia (AML), when bone-marrow aspirate is unobtainable and circulating blasts are absent, myeloid phenotype may be confirmed on a core biopsy by immunohistochemistry.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Conventional cytogenetic analysis is mandatory in the evaluation of AML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute myeloid leukemia (AML), if conventional cytogenetics yields no analyzable metaphases, FISH is an alternative for detecting specified recurrent fusions and myelodysplasia-related chromosome abnormalities.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Myeloblasts, monoblasts, and megakaryoblasts are included in the marrow or blood blast count used for AML classification.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In AML with monocytic or myelomonocytic differentiation, monoblasts and promonocytes are counted as blast equivalents, whereas abnormal monocytes are not.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In AML with PML::RARA or a variant RARA rearrangement, promyelocytes are counted as blast equivalents for classification.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Cases with a history of CML and at least 20% blasts are classified as CML in myeloid blast phase rather than AML with BCR::ABL1.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Remaining cases without a higher-priority AML-defining category are designated MDS/AML otherwise not specified when marrow or blood blasts are 10%-19%.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN AML Recommendations 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Do not apply the 2024 ELN Less-Intensive classification to AML patients who have received prior HMA treatment.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: ELN 2024 Less-Intensive AML Risk Classification

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In CMML, the FAB classification distinguishes myelodysplastic from myeloproliferative disease using a leukocyte-count threshold of 13 × 10^9/L (≤13 × 10^9/L vs >13 × 10^9/L, respectively).
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: CMML-specific CPSS-Mol score

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In CMML, JAK2, NRAS, and SETBP1 mutations were significantly associated with the myeloproliferative subtype (CMML-MP).
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: CMML-specific CPSS-Mol score

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In CMML, TET2 and SF3B1 mutations were significantly associated with the myelodysplastic subtype (CMML-MD; P=.007 and P=.03, respectively).
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: CMML-specific CPSS-Mol score

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For CCUS, MDS and MDS/MPN, cytopenia thresholds are haemoglobin <13 g/dL in males or <12 g/dL in females, ANC <1.8 ×10^9/L, and platelets <150 ×10^9/L.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: CML is defined by the BCR::ABL1 fusion resulting from t(9;22)(q34;q11).
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: CML blast phase is defined by ≥20% myeloid blasts in blood or marrow, extramedullary blast proliferation, or increased lymphoblasts in blood or marrow; accelerated phase is omitted from WHO5.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Major PV diagnostic criteria include elevated haemoglobin and/or haematocrit, marrow panmyelosis with pleomorphic mature megakaryocytes, and JAK2 p.V617F or a JAK2 exon 12 mutation.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: CNL is a BCR::ABL1-negative MPN characterized by sustained neutrophilia with WBC ≥25 ×10^9/L and ≥80% segmented neutrophils/bands, neutrophilic marrow hypercellularity and hepatosplenomegaly.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: CEL is characterized by sustained clonal proliferation of morphologically abnormal eosinophils/eosinophil precursors causing persistent blood and marrow hypereosinophilia.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For CEL, the interval required to define sustained hypereosinophilia is 4 weeks rather than 6 months.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: CEL requires both evidence of clonality and abnormal bone-marrow morphology, such as megakaryocytic or erythroid dysplasia.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For CEL, increased blasts (≥2% in blood or 5–19% in marrow) are no longer an alternative to demonstrating clonality.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Updated JMML criteria require exclusion of KMT2A rearrangements.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: JMML diagnosis emphasizes molecular studies demonstrating RAS-pathway activation together with clinical and laboratory criteria.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In systemic mastocytosis, KIT p.D816V with VAF ≥10% in bone-marrow cells or peripheral-blood leukocytes qualifies as a B-finding.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Any KIT mutation causing ligand-independent activation is accepted as a minor diagnostic criterion for systemic mastocytosis.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Well-differentiated systemic mastocytosis may occur in any systemic-mastocytosis subtype; most cases lack KIT codon 816 mutation and typically show CD25/CD2 negativity with CD30 positivity.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS is defined by cytopenias and morphologic dysplasia, with a recommended dysplasia threshold of 10% for all lineages.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Within genetically defined MDS, MDS with biallelic TP53 inactivation supersedes MDS-5q and MDS-SF3B1 in the WHO5 hierarchy.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In MDS-5q, an SF3B1 mutation or a TP53 mutation that is not multi-hit does not by itself override the MDS-5q diagnosis.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For SF3B1-wild-type MDS with ≥15% ring sideroblasts, “MDS with low blasts and ring sideroblasts” remains an acceptable alternative designation.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: WHO5 retains a 20% blast cutoff to delineate MDS from AML while removing blast cutoffs for most AML types with defining genetic abnormalities.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: CMML requires persistent absolute peripheral-blood monocytosis ≥0.5 ×10^9/L and relative monocytosis ≥10%.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: When absolute monocytosis is ≥0.5 but <1.0 ×10^9/L, CMML diagnosis requires a clonal cytogenetic or molecular abnormality and dysplasia in at least one lineage.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In a patient with monocytosis, a documented MPN history excludes CMML; marrow MPN features and/or a high burden of JAK2, CALR or MPL mutations supports MPN with monocytosis rather than CMML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In a suspected CMML case with eosinophilia, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with tyrosine-kinase gene fusions should be excluded by assessing for PDGFRA rearrangement (most commonly FIP1L1::PDGFRA), PDGFRB rearrangement (most commonly ETV6::PDGFRB), FGFR1 rearrangement, JAK2 rearrangement, FLT3 rearrangement, ETV6::ABL1, and other defined tyrosine-kinase fusions including ETV6::FGFR2, ETV6::LYN, ETV6::NTRK3, RANBP2::ALK, BCR::RET, and FGFR1OP::RET. WHO5 treats PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, JAK2 and FLT3 as rearrangement-defined categories rather than restricting them to a single fusion partner.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: MDS/MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis is redefined on the basis of SF3B1 mutation and renamed MDS/MPN with SF3B1 mutation and thrombocytosis.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For SF3B1-wild-type MDS/MPN with ≥15% ring sideroblasts, “MDS/MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis” remains an acceptable term.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: WHO5 recognizes AML with PML::RARA, RUNX1::RUNX1T1 and CBFB::MYH11 as AML types with defining genetic abnormalities.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML with BCR::ABL1 and AML with CEBPA mutation are the defining-genetic-abnormality AML types that still require at least 20% blasts; for BCR::ABL1 this avoids overlap with CML.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML with KMT2A, MECOM or NUP98 rearrangement may be diagnosed with a blast count below 20%.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML with NPM1 mutation can be diagnosed irrespective of blast count, with clinicopathologic correlation.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML with CEBPA mutation includes biallelic CEBPA mutations and single CEBPA mutations in the basic leucine zipper region.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Somatic RUNX1 mutation is not sufficient to define a standalone WHO5 AML type because it lacks specificity across defining molecular contexts.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: AML, myelodysplasia-related has a mutation-based definition that includes SRSF2, SF3B1, U2AF1, ZRSR2, ASXL1, EZH2, BCOR or STAG2.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Morphologic myelodysplasia alone is no longer sufficient to diagnose AML, myelodysplasia-related.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia, the RAM immunophenotype correlates with CBFA2T3::GLIS2, a subtype of AML with other defined genetic alterations.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Before a diagnosis of CEL is rendered, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with tyrosine-kinase gene fusions must be excluded.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: WHO 5th Edition 2022

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In patients investigated for unexplained cytopenia, a negative result across the studied 40-gene panel did not exclude the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML): the negative predictive value was 0.76, increasing to 0.84 when mutation status was combined with standard karyotyping.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In patients investigated for unexplained cytopenia, finding two or more somatic mutations in the studied 40-gene panel was strongly predictive of the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML), with positive predictive value 0.88 (95% CI 0.84-0.92). These predictive findings were reported as fully confirmed in the independent 190-patient validation cohort.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For mutations measured in isolated peripheral-blood granulocytes, a VAF around 0.10 was associated with the best classification of the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML); the paper cautions that the applicable allele-burden threshold may vary when a different blood-cell source is used. These predictive findings were reported as fully confirmed in the independent 190-patient validation cohort.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In unexplained cytopenia, mutations in SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1, JAK2, or RUNX1 had the highest predictive values for the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML), with positive predictive values of 0.88-0.97 irrespective of co-occurring mutations. These predictive findings were reported as fully confirmed in the independent 190-patient validation cohort.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In unexplained cytopenia, isolated TET2, DNMT3A, or ASXL1 mutations were substantially less predictive of the study's composite myeloid-neoplasm endpoint (MDS, MDS/MPN, MPN, or AML) than the same mutations occurring with additional genetic lesions (positive predictive value 0.29-0.57 vs 0.81-0.89). These predictive findings were reported as fully confirmed in the independent 190-patient validation cohort.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: For patients diagnosed with MDS on the basis of mild dysplasia (<25% dysplastic cells), absence of detectable clonality by standard cytogenetics and targeted sequencing, together with a stable course, raised concern that the MDS diagnosis might be inappropriate despite meeting then-current WHO criteria.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: Primary myelofibrosis with JAK2 co-mutation was the stated specificity exception for SRSF2 or U2AF1: after excluding this pattern, SRSF2 and U2AF1 mutations showed 100% specificity for myeloid neoplasm with myelodysplasia.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In cases with inconclusive dysplasia, highly specific mutation patterns may provide presumptive evidence of MDS even without definitive morphology. The reported patterns included splicing-factor mutations and co-mutation patterns involving TET2, ASXL1, or DNMT3A with RUNX1, EZH2, CBL, BCOR, CUX1, TP53, or IDH1/IDH2; SRSF2/U2AF1 with JAK2 in primary myelofibrosis was a stated specificity exception.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In MDS with del(5q), the chromosomal deletion itself can represent the founding and disease-defining genetic lesion.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: As restated from then-current WHO criteria, MDS diagnosis required unexplained cytopenia plus morphologic evidence of dysplasia and/or an MDS-specific cytogenetic abnormality.
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: Malcovati 2017 CCUS Foundation

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: In MPN, absence of mutations in all three phenotypic driver genes JAK2, CALR, and MPL defines the molecular designation “triple-negative.”
diagnosis_evidence_cards.paper_nickname: DALIAH 2022 MPN genomics

diagnosis_evidence_cards.interpretation: As restated in this paper, bone marrow fibrosis above grade 1 is one of the two main IWG-MRT diagnostic criteria for post-PV/post-ET myelofibrosis.
